# Independent audit: orientation-resolved equality-cap flux

Audited `candidate e81d0f726880ea4a`, including
its balanced version and facet-free exposed-hull consequence.
Result: PASS. The exact verifier
`supporting computation verify_orientation_resolved_facet_flux.py` was rerun successfully.

## One-sided signs and ambient affine pivots

Write the cap as L>=0 with unit continuous normal. An empty supporting
fiber lies in L<=0, whereas a full supporting fiber lies in L>=0.
For g=h-h(y_e), the exact derivatives are:

    empty side: right integral g_+, left integral min(g,0);
    full side:  right integral min(g,0), left integral g_+.

These signs agree with both gain into the original empty cap and loss
from the original full cap. The rotating-plane coordinates give the
threshold -t g_0/(1+t b), whose denominator is positive near zero and
does not change its first-order velocity. The original unit-normal
fiber coordinates have Jacobian one, so the full proper section
measure A and all displayed coarea factors are correct.

On a positive-area supporting face, convex interpolation and bounded
slice compactness give its one-sided section limit. Proper section
relative boundaries are null as well. Uniformly bounded threshold
velocities and bounded projected support supply domination. A
zero-area face contributes o(|t|). For d=1 this reduces exactly to
the clipped-interval endpoint rule with H_0 section measure one.

At endpoint zero use the actual LEFT derivative, which is <=0;
at endpoint one use the actual RIGHT derivative, which is >=0.
Their difference is therefore nonnegative and equals

    -A + integral_E dist(h,[0,1])
       - integral_F [1+dist(h,[0,1])].

The pointwise identities remain exact at h=0 and h=1. Thus the
new inequality uses genuine one-sided minima; it does not select
independent favorable Clarke traces. The ambient h formulation
also correctly includes distinct points in the same integer fiber.

## Balanced circuit and calibration

Each actual critical cap can first be normalized to unit continuous
normal; its positive circuit coefficients can then be rescaled to
balance those unit normals. Multiplying the one-cap inequalities
by these positive coefficients is valid with the same ambient h.
Different faces and bases remain explicitly labeled, so no false
normal-balance cancellation of their measures is introduced.

For the layered cube, the downward cap has all 5^n-3^n supporting
sections on the empty side and exterior charge 5^(n-1). The opposite
cap puts all those sections on the full side. Its necessary left
side is exactly 3^n+(5^n-3^n)+5^(n-1)>0, with right side zero.
This correctly rules out the opposite cap as a simultaneous minimizer
at the two candidates, for every T>0. It does not exclude all other
possible directions or a different global plateau.

## Facet-free exposed maximizing bases

The additional geometric conclusion is valid. A positive margin at
another global maximizer permits a strict own-fiber slab reduction;
a zero margin gives a common minimizing cap and contradicts A>0
when all supporting section measures vanish. Thus every attaining
cap strictly excludes every other distinct maximizing point.

An integer convex combination of maximizing bases, lifted by the
same weights to their full points, would again maximize depth. Its
attaining cap has strictly negative margin at every distinct point
participating in a nontrivial combination, contradicting its zero
margin at their average. This proves the empty-lattice-hull and
vertex assertions, including the case that the average coincides
with one participating point. The balanced active circuit at each
maximizer cancels its continuous coefficients and gives the claimed
strict exposing functional on the finite base set. The single-point
case is harmless.

These conclusions explicitly require the facet-free hypothesis.
The note leaves the general faceted global-maximizer problem open
within this investigation and claims no OC bound.

## Precise limit of cross-cap coverage

A rigorous transfer consequence is recorded separately in
`candidate cdad0ee8b68e978a`.
At a positive fiber, discard ALL caps with zero local d-volume;
the remaining finite closed caps still cover its entire interior
and hence its closure. Every empty supporting face is therefore
covered by positive-volume recipient caps, and its nonnegative
weighted face measure is bounded by the sum of recipient TRACES
on that face.

Those recipients need not lie in the balanced critical circuit
through the chosen candidate pair. Moreover coverage alone does not
bound these traces by the recipients' own section measures: the
explicit triangle in the companion note has an empty face of length
2 but complementary proper recipient sections of length 2epsilon
each. This identifies the exact additional comparison still needed;
no cross-cap mass cancellation follows from the proved flux formulas.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
